why: The one statement of the durable-wallpaper reference rule; docs/architecture/wallpaper.md states it in prose. `ref` and `resolve` are run by both scripts/test-wallpaper-refs.py against bin/vshell_helper.py and scripts/test-wallpaper-refs.js against quickshell/vshell/Common/Paths.qml, so those two cannot drift apart without one going red. `recover` is the helper's alone: repairing a background another installation recorded needs the filesystem, so the shell carries no such rule.
refWhy: Recording: portable_ref, and resolved as the round trip back through resolve_path. One containment test, so a path this installation does not own is recorded as it stands even when `present` says this installation holds that package: recording never consults the filesystem, and repairing is the read side's job.

ref.why: a built-in package's background under the running root becomes a rooted reference
anything else under the root is rooted too, such as the branding image a hook falls back to
a user package does not move with the shell, so its background stays absolute
a path another installation wrote is recorded as it stands even though this installation holds that very package; repairing it is the helper's read side
a directory outside VGS shaped like a package is recorded as it stands, since recording is containment alone
a picture the user chose outside VGS is left alone
a system wallpaper outside both roots is left alone
the colour literal setWallpaperColor stores in the same field is not a path
a reference already in reference form is recorded unchanged and still resolves

resolveWhy: The resolver alone: resolve_path, on every reference form durable state carries.

resolve.why: a rooted reference resolves against the root the shell is running from
a home-relative reference, the form target destinations are written in, resolves too
an absolute path is already resolved
no reference resolves to no path

recoverWhy: Reading: resolved_wallpaper, which repairs before resolving. Each row names the package files the reading installation holds, under `present`, relative to whichever root the row says. A path inside the user's packages answers as it stands; every other absolute path with a package background's tail is looked for under the running root and then under the user's packages, and a row whose file is in neither must come back untouched.

recover.why: a background recorded by a checkout that is gone names this installation's copy
a package this installation keeps as a user package answers from there
a reader whose root holds no packages at all, as the greeter's staged runtime does not, changes nothing
a directory outside VGS shaped like a package names no package here, so the file that loads keeps loading
a package name this installation has, under a file name it does not, is not a match
a path under the user's packages answers as it stands, whatever the running root carries
a path under neither root that both roots carry answers from the running root first
a user package is this installation's own and is never repaired
a background under the running root whose own file is gone answers from the user's copy
a rooted reference needs no repair and resolves
a picture outside VGS naming no package is left alone
no wallpaper reads back as nothing
